message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Test build backend

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "backend/**"

  push:
    branches:
      - master
    paths:
      - "backend/**"

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [22.x]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      - name: Cache node modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: backend/node_modules
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-node-${{ matrix.node-version }}-modules-${{ hashFiles('backend/package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-node-${{ matrix.node-version }}-modules-

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: backend
        run: npm install

      - run: npm run build
        working-directory: backend",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs `npm install` on every run with no dependency cache, so repeated CI runs re-fetch and reinstall backend dependencies. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (cache dependency downloads) applies: repeated dependency fetching is measurable from the CI history, the cache input is the lockfile plus runner/Node environment, and the existing install/build steps are preserved unchanged. Adding `actions/cache@v4` for `backend/node_modules`, keyed by `backend/package-lock.json` with a restore fallback, shortens warm runs while keeping a full `npm install` on cache misses. No permissions are weakened, no secrets or deployment steps are added, and no new network access beyond the existing npm install is introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]
}
